abstract: The Test pattern generator (TPGs) is one of the prominent components in any testing environment and decides the overall system performance digital circuits functional verification and emerging steadily in recent years to accommodate highly complex system designs; however significant performance gap still exists in existing TPG modules to meet the design constraints associated to the different system in terms of maximum allowable testing power and fault coverage etc. in this paper novel energy efficient Switch Controlled state transition-based LFSR TPG is introduced to formulate test patterns with maximum length and randomness. Here LFSR generated test vectors using conventional LFSR reseeding model with fixed polynomial configuration is divided and grouped into smaller blocks and used Switch Controlled encoding process to transforming into multiple independent test pattern blocks. The concatenation of these isolated encoder generated blocks improves the randomness in final test vector sequence which also includes transitional and non- transitional values to control the overall switching activity. Moreover, in accordance with the power constrains associated to each binary positions of test vectors some weightages are assigned to control certain bit transitions which can significantly optimize the dynamic power consumption during testing process. Finally Switch controller is used to regulate the state transition with maximal randomness characteristics compared with other LFSR. Here both clock rate and number state in Switch Controlled machine can be dynamically changed to modify the LFSR statistics in accordance with BIST requirements. The proposed work is successfully synthesized in Quartos-II environment tool and based on simulated results for TPG with LFSR the power has been optimized by 3% and the hardware utilization is minimized by 7%

articleTitle: Implications of continual learning for lesion of the skin categorizing and detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Development of techniques that can gradually learn from new samples is now important due to the growing number of data. Training a network with new data poses challenges, including the phenomenon known as "catastrophic forgetting." This occurs when a network's performance on previously learned data drops as it tries to learn from new instances. To address the issue of catastrophic forgetting, the article includes a powerful approach known as experience replay. Investigations are conducted on different datasets to analyze the impact of catastrophic forgetting. The technique is compared against various approaches, including individual training, mutual training, and fine-tuning. When compared to the fine-tuning approach, the model using experience replay retains knowledge from the previous dataset, leading to a 13% increase in accuracy.

articleTitle: Revamping nodes for Energy efficient Clustering in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Clustering in WSN groups nodes into clusters managed by a designated cluster head to improve network performance and coordination, ultimately transmitting data to the sink node. The LEACH protocol, a well-known standard, enables efficient clustering in wireless sensor networks. An alternative protocol, balanced cluster formation, offers the benefit of equal-sized clusters but with some overlap between them. This paper sets forth a hybrid node revamping scheme Energy-efficient uniform size clustering (EUSC) that balances load, improves lifespan, maintains uniform cluster size, and avoids cluster overlap in wireless sensor networks. The proposed solution Improves clustering accuracy by considering node density and extends network lifespan by refreshing clusters based on both the next-best cluster head and node energy levels.

articleTitle: Enhanced RPL-Based Routing with Mobility Support in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: the Internet of Things has become an unprecedented technology that connects billions of objects and makes a wide range of applications. The substantial expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has surpassed the capacity of traditional routing protocols to handle the vast number of nodes. Consequently, the Routing Protocol for Low-power and Lossy Networks (RPL) has been created and extensively adopted in IoT networks. Traditional RPL are having static characteristics, however, it is less useful in situations where mobile IoT devices are involved. This article explores the challenges raised by mobility in IoT networks and a novel approach for enhancing RPL is proposed to properly incorporate mobile nodes in the network. The suggested remedy makes use of adaptive techniques to provide optimal routing while taking into account the adaptability of mobile IoT devices.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Hand gesture detection, which is adaptable and user-friendly, is one of the most active study areas in the field of human-computer interfaces. Using the gesture recognition system, a system is designed that can be deployed to communicate with disabled people or to administer a product. Excellent internal consistency commonalities in hand gesture postures, slight variances, non-uniform surroundings, with user-specific hand form and shape variations all offer considerable obstacles to creating an efficient hand gesture detection mechanism. In this article a hand gesture detection method which is user independent is examined using custom characteristics such convolutional neural networks (CNN). A technology known as Gesture Recognition uses mathematical algorithms to interpret human gestures. The dataset is collected and stored in the form of files and folders. Using CNN algorithm, the collected dataset is compared with the threshold value of the given input and thus the result is presented in the form of text or voice. Gesture Recognition System is an inventive user interface that eliminates the challenges associated with using remote controls for home appliances by replacing the remote-control system with hand gestures. Deep learning and computer vision are two tools that can be used to further the cause. Using the suggested method, an authentic implementation of gesture - based system is constructed and evaluated.

articleTitle: A Comparative Survey on Paddy Leaf Diseases Detection using Convolutional Neural Network Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Despite recent difficulties in rice cultivation, rice leaf diseases are still identified using traditional methods. This leads to a fall in production of the crops. Initial detection allows farmers to increase output rates and efficiently take the necessary treatment measures. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithms’ quick development has significantly modified agricultural practices, particularly in disease identification. This paper comprehensively examines the use of CNN-based approaches for identifying illnesses in rice leaves. Given the rising need for rice production and quality on a global scale, accurate and quick disease diagnosis is essential. This review study also deals with the different CNN architectures and the corresponding modifications to detect rice disease. It also includes single - and multi-class classification algorithms. In addition, examining important datasets, preprocessing methods, and augmentation strategies reveals their impact on the performance of the developed models. Comparative evaluations of the surveyed papers highlight the potential and constraints of various CNN models and suggest fresh directions for investigations. This study highlights the potential of CNNs to completely reinvent across automated and effective verification, which ultimately increases agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Nanosheet Junctionless FET for switching applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)

articleTitle: High Performance VLSI Architecture for Real-Time Video Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: In the field of video processing, edge detection plays a crucial role in various applications such as object recognition, scene understanding, and video surveillance. Real-time processing of video data demands efficient hardware architectures that can handle the computational load of edge detection algorithms while maintaining low power consumption. This paper presents a novel VLSI (Very-Large-Scale Integration) architecture tailored for real-time video edge detection. The proposed architecture is designed to achieve a balance between high-performance edge detection and resource-efficient implementation. It leverages parallel processing and optimized data flow to enhance computational speed. Furthermore, careful consideration is given to memory management and data buffering to ensure seamless video stream processing. The architecture is based on Canny edge detection algorithms and implemented on Artix 7. The proposed architecture also implemented on GPP to validate performance of VLSI Architecture.

articleTitle: Live Telecasting Robo using Arduino Uno
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: As we know that now days robots place a crucial role in technology and as well as in our lives. A remote-operated robot is a wheeled device that can be controlled from a distance, enabling users to navigate and interact with their environment through its wireless internet connectivity. Usually, the robot utilizes a tablet or smart phone to offer video and audio functionalities, as well as to provide a visual representation of remote locations. Our paper combines a smart phone that creates a virtual reality experience through its screen and a quadrupedal robotic vehicle. The vehicle can be controlled using an Arduino Bluetooth app, allowing users to maneuver and interact with their virtual environment. The camera movement is controlled by servo motor and data processed by the Arduino board. Specified link is generated by Arduino and by using this link a video is received by the smart phone. Using an Arduino, a camera placed at a distant location is used to visually record the environment. These images are accessible on our devices. Additionally, the newly added capability gives customers a real-time experience by allowing the camera to move in the same direction as their phones. In indoor environments like hospitals and museums, the cost-effective telepresence robotic platform with Arduino and suggestive feedback and real-time feeling for the user offers complete and immersive remote operation. Using remote connectivity to make live feeds accessible in dangerous locations like conflict hotspots, dusty regions, nuclear explosion zones, or industrial hazardous zones. Our paper addresses the challenge of immersion in Telepresence Robotic systems by integrating Virtual Reality headsets, such as Google Cardboard. This allows users to have a more immersive experience while remotely controlling the robot. We have also implemented online real-time head movement control, enabling natural head movements to be reflected in the remote environment. By combining these features with traditional telepresence platforms, controlled remotely and wirelessly via the Internet, we offer a comprehensive solution that revolutionizes the telepresence robotics field.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis on SVM-based Image Classifiers for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: The Image processing is still being focused by the experts as one a thrust area. The different applications of the Image processing provide wide benefits to the society in their day to day life. The classification technique in the image processing is one of the robust approaches which are used, machine to understand and categorize the images automatically. This provides wide benefits to the industry such as satellite communication, telemedicine, cargo services, and entertainment. In this paper the contemporary techniques available in the image classification techniques are surveyed in detail and some of the classification techniques such as Support Vector Machine algorithm are verified using the Matlab tool to analyses its accuracy. The simulated outcomes are represented numerically as well as graphically for better understanding.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Pre-processing Techniques and Image Datasets for Lung Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Lung cancer is a devastating illness that affects people all over the world. As a result, accurate and earlier prediction of lung cancer is critical for improving disease prognosis in patients. To identify lung nodule growth, many studies have been developed using various imaging modalities. Deep Learning (DL) techniques are used in this work for preprocessing, noise reduction, and classification. This paper focuses on cutting-edge ways for maximizing decision analysis as picture modalities, dataset pre-processing, and Deep Neural Networks (DNN) are employed for lung nodule classification. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have recently been utilized in conjunction with DNN for classification purposes. This extensive study provides a greater understanding of how to improve future studies for efficiently predicting lung cancer.

articleTitle: Fake Review Detection using Evidential Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Online shopping is a major part of our lives and has proven to make our lives easier and more time-saving. Rating and reviewing those online products is how we spread the word and also get to know about a product’s quality. Ratings help the e-commerce sites rank the products in a category, and that’s how we purchase the best possible product. This affects a business, as the better the reviews, the more consumers there are and the higher the profit. On the negative side, we have human spammers and machine-generated automatic spamming of reviews and ratings, which can affect any business positively or negatively and would also create a false image of a product, leading to a bad customer experience. Therefore, if we are able to find a classifier that can tell us if a review is fake or real, it can help online shopping sites determine a product’s actual ratings and thus reduce unfair competition. Hence, in this paper, we propose the classification of reviews via the Dempster-Shafer (DS) evidential classifier. This classifier has proven to be very effective in classifying images and texts. This paper mainly focuses on how certain features, when fed to the Dempster-Shafer classifier, can help us detect fake reviews.

articleTitle: Priority-Induced Round-robin scheduling algorithm with dynamic time quantum for Cloud computing environment
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Cloud computing provides a virtual platform that allows resources to be accessed through the Internet. As cloud environment needs to serve multiple requests, efficient task scheduling is required to maintain its performance. Round Robin Scheduling algorithm is one of the most employed algorithms for task scheduling in cloud environment. In this paper, an improved Round Robin algorithm has been proposed. The proposed algorithm introduces dynamic time quantum and priority for scheduling the tasks. It is carried out by categorizing the tasks based on their urgency to complete the task from the ready queue. A comparative study is also established and inferred that the proposed algorithm is comparatively enhanced and is optimum for the Cloud Computing environment.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection and Marker-Based Watershed Segmentation for Size Estimation using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Brain tumors are a common and severe malignant tumor condition that can reduce one's life if not diagnosed early enough. The categorization of brain tumors is a difficult task. Furthermore, when there is a huge amount of data to be assisted, it is a challenging work. Because brain tumors vary in appearance and share similarities with normal tissues, it is challenging to isolate tumor regions. In this algorithm, we suggested a model that first uses a convolutional neural network and classical classifiers, then uses the Fuzzy C-Means clustering approach to remove brain tumors from 2D MRI brain scans. The structure of available data sets, brain tumors, component extraction, augmentation techniques, Transfer Learning (TL), Deep Learning (DL) classification, and reinforcement learning (RL) are also examined in this work.

articleTitle: Reduction of Frequent Link Disconnection Problem for Reliable Connection in Internet of Vehicles (IoV)
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) represent a novel wireless technology wherein mobile vehicles function as nodes, establishing a dynamic network while in motion at varying velocities. However, the rapid changes in topology present serious challenges, with Frequent Link Disconnection being a major problem. Despite various routing protocols designed for VANETs, finding an efficient and effective solution that addresses all aspects remains problematic. This paper suggests a Regularized Zone-based Routing Protocol (RZRP) as an improvement to the Zone Routing Protocol to address these problems. The main objective is to provide connection reliability in applications for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). RZRP reduces the amount of network overhead and reaction times by finding stable routes with the use of a QoS algorithm that considered speed, destination, and delay. The protocol also considers vehicle speed and direction to avoid link disconnection due to barriers. Incorporating an empirical Information-based Clustering Algorithm within the zone, RZRP maintains the cluster structure while meeting quality of service requirements as the network evolves. The protocol's experimental validation will be carried out by using several criteria, and found that it attains 26% of routing overhead, 98% of packet delivery ratio,11% of link failures and 21% of average end to end delay.

articleTitle: Object-Based Key Frame Extraction in Videos
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Due to the significant improvements in communication and network infrastructure, there is a tremendous exchange of visual data. The process of watching videos is time-consuming to the user. It requires an immediate solution to extract the meaningful parts of the video, reducing the user’s time and computational storage. In this paper, an object-based video summarization process is proposed. Object detection is done by training a CNN-based object detection model known as the You Only Look Once (YOLO V5) model. Detection is followed by an object-tracking method known as the Kalman filtering algorithm. The saliency score for each object in the frame is computed based on the various objects including motion, the centrality of an object, and other color-based features. The method is evaluated on benchmark datasets namely Open Video Project (OVP) and the custom-made video dataset. It has achieved precision, recall and F-score better than the state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method reduces computational time significantly.

articleTitle: Survey and Analysis of Real-Time Face Detection Techniques in Video Scenes: Current Advancements and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: In an era of rapid advancements in computer vision, the field of real-time face detection within video scenes has witnessed remarkable progress, igniting applications across diverse sectors like surveillance, human-computer interaction, and augmented reality. This paper presents an exhaustive review of recent strides in this domain, embracing an extensive spectrum of methodologies, techniques, and applications. The review commences by delving into the core concepts underpinning face detection, explicating the multifaceted challenges posed by fluctuating lighting, diverse poses, expressions, and potential obstructions. A meticulous exploration of both classical and contemporary approaches unfolds, with classical methods such as the Viola-Jones cascade, celebrated for its historical significance and enduring utility, alongside an in-depth analysis of cutting-edge deep learning models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), region-based CNNs, and one-shot detectors, revealing the architectures and mechanisms that empower these models to achieve unprecedented levels of accuracy and speed. Additionally, the research offers a discerning assessment of benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics, instrumental in impartially gauging and contrasting diverse methodologies, leveraging the ascendancy of annotated datasets for data-driven model refinement and validation. Contemporary applications that leverage real-time face detection are explored, illuminating its pivotal role in surveillance systems, video analytics, and human-computer interaction, underscored by its integration with allied computer vision tasks like facial recognition and emotion analysis, accentuating its interdisciplinary essence and real-world pertinence. This research not only navigates through recent breakthroughs in real-time face detection within video scenes but also equips researchers and practitioners with invaluable insights into the potentials, limitations, and future trajectories in this dynamic field, poised for further innovation driven by increasingly sophisticated algorithms and the burgeoning computational resources at our disposal, thereby resonating across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Sustainable Education System Using Vedic Scripture and Cyber Security
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: An artificial intelligence-enabled maintainable instruction framework that consolidates Vedic scripture and cybersecurity measures has the potential to revolutionize the way we learn and instruct. This framework can give personalized and long lasting learning encounters, advance virtual and collaborative learning, and encourage moral and feasible learning. By leveraging the control of AI and other developing innovations, this framework can make a more comprehensive, available, and maintainable instruction framework. Be that as it may, there are a number of challenges with this framework, counting issues with information security and protection, moral issues, and the prerequisite for major framework and innovation ventures. In spite of these challenges, the system’s future viewpoints are promising, and it has the potential to plan learners for the challenges and openings of the long run.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Techniques Integrated UAV for Next Generation Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: With agriculture accounting for over 17% of the country’s GDP and the majority of Indians’ primary source of income, it is one of the most vital industries in India. The world population is increasing every year and this requires an efficient agriculture system to meet the ever increasing demands. Such a system would not be feasible without the use of computational tools and forecasting strategies. Covid19 pandemic and climate change pose serious threats to the agriculture industry and hence we should make use of technologies like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) which can bring huge transformation in the agriculture sector. Agricultural robots can be deployed on farms for crop and soil monitoring and UAVs are capable of spraying water for irrigation purposes without human intervention. This paper illustrates the benefits of integrating AI with Agriculture and thereby opening doors to next generation agriculture.

articleTitle: Kidney Abnormalities Prediction in Ultrasound Images using Transfer Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Transfer Learning Algorithm is becoming popular for medical image analysis, because it has high level of flexibility in dealing with Image dataset with minimum number of Images. It makes convenient for researchers to test and train medical images, assign the determined weights thus reducing the computational complexities and pre-processing time. Presence of stones, tumour, cyst and other kidney abnormalities in Kidney Ultrasound Images is a challenging task for a radiologist. There exists a difference of opinion between an experienced physician and a beginner in the field of urology and nephrology. Requirement of an intelligent tool for diagnosis in the medical field has increased in the recent years due to the enormous growth of Artificial Intelligent and Machine Learning algorithms. In this proposed work Pretrained Efficient Net models B1-B5 are used with the pretrained weights of ImageNet data set thus, reducing the pre-processing time taken for random initialization of weights. Ultrasound Kidney Image Dataset are taken as inputs for training phase and testing Phase. Fine Tuning is adapted by changing the hyper parameter setting. Performance metrics such asF1Score and AUC are evaluated. Efficient Net B4 Model gives satisfactory result in terms of AUC as 89.95% and F1 Score 82.9%. Cross validation when carried out by training the models with predetermined weights of CT scan Kidney Images resulted in improving AUC to 90.9% for the prediction of kidney stones, cyst and tumour.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning Algorithms for Accurate Ovarian Cancer Diagnosis: A State-of-the-Art Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Ovarian cancer, a dangerous health problem affecting women everywhere, need for improved diagnostic and prognostic methods. In this research, deep convolutional neural networks are used to focus a thorough exploration of machine learning methods applied to proteomic and imaging datasets. Our research, which included articles published between 2016 and 2023, showed that machine learning algorithms, be able to significantly rise the precision of ovarian cancer identification, prognosis, and treatment response prediction. This review explains how deep CNNs can categorize ovarian cancer tumors effectively in comparison to other approaches. Furthermore, we offer a comparative analysis of several machine learning methods, such as K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Networks, that are utilized to diagnose ovarian cancer. Our results highlight how deeply effective deep learning techniques are at producing superior diagnostic results.

articleTitle: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting to Forecast Weight Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: This paper represents a multivariate time series forecasting approach to predict the weight dynamics of an insect colony. In this paper, we are predicting the Colony Weight of the Insect which has the main impact on the growth and overall health of the insects. To accomplish this task, we have performed extensive preprocessing on the time series data, ensuring data quality and suitability for analysis. Overall, we have conducted a high-level Exploratory Data Analysis which covers time series analysis to identify different patterns as well as trends present in the time series data. Following the EDA, Feature Engineering and Feature Selection techniques have also been performed to find the features that have an impact on the colony weight feature. As a follow-up, we have performed Multivariate Time Series forecasting of the colony weight for future data with Time Series Forecasting techniques such as Vector Autoregressive moving average with exogenous regressors (VARMAX) and with Deep Learning techniques such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Several statistical parameters such as AIC score, BIC score as well as MSE value along with the grid search method have been utilized to find the optimal lag value which affects the model performance significantly. The performance of the black box model has been compared with the interpretable model to find the best outcome. This paper contributes to the field of multivariate time series forecasting in the context of insect colony dynamics. Various insights that have been gained from that study have implications for understanding insect behaviour, population dynamics, and overall ecosystem health. Furthermore, the proposed methodology can be extended to other domains involving multivariate time series forecasting.

articleTitle: Smart Railway Infrastructure: Fusion of IoT, RFID and VANET for Enhanced Safety and Operational Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: The existing railway systems face significant challenges in terms of safety, operational efficiency, and sustainability. One of the critical concerns is the risk of train collisions, which can have severe consequences for passengers, railway infrastructure, and the environment. Additionally, there is a growing need to explore alternative sources of energy to reduce dependence on traditional power grids. Enhancing railway safety and efficiency, our paper integrates IoT, RFID, and VANET technologies. By combining real-time monitoring, asset tracking, and predictive maintenance, it revolutionizes railway systems. Our paper includes piezoelectric plates for energy harvesting, ultrasonic sensors for track integrity, and VANET for seamless communication. This comprehensive solution promises safer travel and improved operations, underlining our commitment to a smart and secure railway network.

articleTitle: Enhancing Taiwan Guava Grading through Advanced Image Processing and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Grading unique fruits like Taiwan guavas has historically relied heavily on specialized human examination of visual and textural characteristics. This dependence on inconsistent manual inspection incurs massive inefficiencies across guava harvesting, sorting, sales and processing operations. The lack of rapid, precise and standardized grading practices results in improper quality evaluation, revenue losses for farmers and inadequate transparency for consumers regarding produce freshness and safety. This pioneering research aims to overcome these challenges by developing an advanced computer vision system tailored to automate the visual grading process for Taiwan guavas. A large and diverse dataset of guava images representing natural variations in shape, size, color, texture and defects is systematically compiled. This dataset is leveraged to optimize a state-of-the-art deep neural network model using techniques like transfer learning and data augmentation. Comprehensive benchmarking experiments demonstrate that the optimized model achieves 89% test accuracy in classifying guavas into industry-standard grades based on quality parameters learned from visual cues. The model operates with high precision and recall, with minimal confusion between adjacent grades. The proposed computer vision-based solution can potentially bring immense benefits in efficiency, consistency, transparency, sustainability and value across guava harvesting, sorting, logistics and sales. Automated grading ensures only premium quality guavas reach consumers, thereby improving farmer incomes and customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Pretrained Encoder-Decoder Transformer Models for Extreme Text Summarization
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Text summarization plays a pivotal role in condensing crucial information from huge volumes of text. This study investigates the utilization of pre-trained transformer models within the domain of text summarization, with a specific emphasis on extreme summarization. It delves into the effectiveness of two prominent models, text-to-text transfer transformers and bidirectional and auto-regressive transformers, when applied to the task of summarization, providing a comparative analysis of their capabilities. The experiments conducted in this study involve the utilization of the XSum and SciTLDR datasets. While fine-tuning T5 and BART on summarization tasks is a standard approach, we delve into the performance of these models without fine-tuning. Additionally, we explore the potential of other pretrained models, such as PREGASUS and distilBART, in generating concise and coherent summaries. This study contributes to the understanding of how pre-trained transformer models can be harnessed effectively for text summarization, especially in extreme summarization scenarios. The findings shed light on the performance, challenges, and potential of these models, opening avenues for further research in the field of automatic text summarization.

articleTitle: Preserving Privacy in Next Keyword Prediction using Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Federated learning has emerged as a ground-breaking approach for collaborative model training across decentralized devices, addressing the challenges of centralized data storage and privacy concerns. In the context of recommendation systems, federated learning enables the creation of personalized recommendations while upholding user privacy. This paper introduces the "FedScope Recommendation System" (FRS) designed to predict next keywords. FRS leverages FedScope architecture which enhances the flexibility and enables the development of a tailored recommendation system. By adopting the modular aspects of FedScope, FRS crafts a recommendation system aligned with the client-server cluster's unique requirements. The proposed FRS serves as an innovative illustration of how federated learning can revolutionize personalized recommendations while maintaining privacy and security.

articleTitle: Enabling Efficient Monitoring in Smart Grid Distribution Systems using IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: This work presents an innovative method for enabling effective monitoring in Internet of Things (IoT) based smart grid distribution systems. With the increasing complexity and dynamic nature of modern power distribution networks, there is a growing need for real-time monitoring and control mechanisms to ensure reliable and efficient energy distribution. The proposed system leverages IoT technology to create a network of interconnected devices, sensors, and communication infrastructure within the smart grid distribution system. Real-time data on multiple parameters, including voltage, current, power quality, and system stability, is gathered and transmitted by these devices. The IoT-based system enables seamless integration and communication between the different components of the smart grid, facilitating comprehensive monitoring and control capabilities. The proposed smart grid includes a high-performance Single Ended Primary Inductance Converter (SEPIC) with a Firefly-optimized Artificial Neural Network (FF-ANN) for maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Together with the stable output voltage, this algorithm effectively keeps an eye on other variables like maximum voltage and current. The performance and efficiency of smart grid distribution systems could be greatly improved by the suggested IoT-based monitoring system.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Aquaculture Surveillance System for Enhanced Fisheries Resource Management
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Assessing water quality parameters is vital for sustainable aquaculture practices, as they have a direct influence on the well-being and productivity of aquatic organisms. Monitoring these parameters in real time is essential for evaluating the health of fish farms, and the emergence of smart solutions utilizing advanced sensors, communication technologies, and the Internet of Things (IoT) emphasizes the increasing importance of water parameter monitoring. Without an effective monitoring and management system, fish farmers lack knowledge of crucial water parameters, rely on outdated health checking methods, and face the risk of fish mortality due to unpredictable weather and environmental factors. This study demonstrates the application of an Internet of Things (IoT) and GPRS SMS communication technology, enables real-time monitoring and timely notifications for farmers regarding the quality parameters of the pond and water resource. This study presented the findings of average water parameter monitoring results in a fishpond study environment, including temperature $(30.35^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$, dissolved oxygen (2.53 mg/L), potential hydrogen (pH) (7.73), and ammonia concentration (5.46 ppm). Additionally, the study assesses the accuracy of the sensors used, with the dissolved oxygen sensor achieving 90%, the pH sensor achieving 92%, and the temperature sensor achieving 96% accuracy.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Framework for Oral Cancer Classification Using Ant Bee Colony Optimization with Support Vector Machine Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Oral cancer (OC) the eighth-fastest spreading malignancy that is currently wreaking havoc on humans, is the one with the highest prevalence in the globe. It is a deadly, widespread malignancy with a high mortality rate. The malignant tumor occurs in several oral regions. It might be difficult for a doctor to diagnose oral cancer. In the field of medicine, novel methods are frequently employed for the categorization and early diagnosis of cancer. The early identification of sickness is a crucial task in the medical domain. The use of classification algorithm plays a crucial role in disease classification. Various hybridized versions of machine learning algorithm along with optimization techniques were used to recognize the disease in its earliest stages. In the proposed strategy, SVM classifier of the machine learning technique and ABCO algorithm were used to classify the resulting features of oral cancer which were produced by feature segmentation and feature extraction process. When the generated results were compared to SVM, the hybrid Ant Bee Colony Optimization Support Vector Machine (ABCOSVM) or MOSVM algorithm outperformed with 99.8% accuracy.

articleTitle: Security Enhancement using Image Hotspot with Hidden Privacy-Cipher text Policy-Attribute Based Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Cloud computing is one of the developing fields for the automation and maintenance of several organizations. It increases the flexibility of the applications and has improved their efficiency. Due to this, a greater number of clients opt for cloud computing. Though it has several advantages in terms of maintenance and functioning of the applications, there is always the issue of data security and reliability. Various research works have concentrated on the security aspect of cloud computing and have proposed different protocols and algorithms to provide the user with the necessary security. However, these security solutions are primarily software-based and lack a basic architecture for protecting the data from malicious attacks. With the development of cryptography and other encryption models, it is difficult for attackers to decrypt the data and provide the necessary solution. This paper uses these advancements to provide a better security model that uses attribute-based encryption to protect user data. The cipher text policy is also used as a standard for this encryption process, and the user is given full control over his data. The file uploading is protected using the HP-CP-ABE method for secured file uploading. The authority center is maintained to authenticate the users in the system. And finally, an image shield security system is used to secure the users’ login. And finally, an OTP verification process is for approving the user. The proposed security model provides a foolproof mechanism to safeguard user security by providing security at different levels. The efficiency of the proposed system is compared with various existing ones, and the usability of the model is validated. The validation clearly shows that the proposed model provides better security than the existing ones.

articleTitle: Advancements in Interstitial Lung Disease Classification and Segmentation: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Interstitial lung disorders, collectively affecting the interstitium around lung air sacs, are marked by fibrosis, inflammation, and compromised lung function. Conditions like Sarcoidosis, Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis, Connective tissue disease-associated ILDs, Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), and more fall under this group. Diagnosis includes clinical assessment, radiographic imaging (e.g., High-Resolution Computed Tomography), lung function tests, and histological lung tissue analysis. Radiologists face difficulties identifying ILDs via X-rays and CT scans, necessitating robust detection, treatment, and monitoring algorithms. Moreover, this review looks into CT scan-related challenges in ILD identification, including image artifacts, data variability, and deep learning model interpretability. By presenting insights and addressing hurdles, this literature review aims to advance important research in medical imaging, particularly in the context of ILD identification.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Microbiome-Disease Association Data using GANs
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: This study evaluates the proficiency of four Generative Adversarial Network models in synthesizing datasets related to microbiome-disease associations. Utilizing the comprehensive Human Microbe Disease Association Database as a foundational resource, a multifaceted evaluative approach is employed, incorporating statistical rigor and visual analytics. While CTGAN and Copula GAN are originally designed for tabular data generation, this study aims to extend the capabilities of WGAN-GP and Vanilla GAN to explore their applicability in the same context. Results reveal that while specialized tabular GANs are adept at encapsulating intricate data patterns, the adaptively employed GANs also manifest commendable promise. The study serves as a robust analytical framework, furnishing valuable insights for ongoing and future research in the realm of microbiome-disease data synthesis.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on using English ASR Models for Leveraging Medical Speech Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Though many deep learning based Automatic Speech Recognition algorithms (ASR) exist, developing a Medical Speech Recognition (MSR) system has many challenges. One such difficulty is that it requires huge annotated data for training a machine learning model to understand the medical vocabulary. As these corpora are not available publicly, this poses a great challenge in MSR development. Recently transfer learning has become popular where a pre-trained model for a task can be leveraged to do another similar task. This work examines the use of pretrained English ASR models to develop a MSR model. A controlled study has been carried out to find the potential opportunities and gaps in using English ASR models such as wav2vec, XLSR and Deepspeech in identification of medical terms from medical sentences. As these models work well for general English transcription, these models are tested with medical sentences spoken by a single speaker with varying tones and speeds and the word error for medical terms is evaluated. Among the models tested, XLSR a multilingual model outperforms the others in identifying the medical terms. From this study it is observed that building a MSR with limited data is feasible by fine-tuning specific layers with transfer learning approach.

articleTitle: Systematic Development of Modified Hybrid Learning based Detection Scheme for White Blood Cancer Cells using Medical Image Processing Methodology with IoT Alert Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: The automated detection of white blood cell cancers like cancer and lymphoma is an active area of medicinal study that presents significant challenges. In this research, we unveil a brand-new, cutting-edge tool for aiding in the diagnosis of disorders affecting the white blood cells. In this work, we propose Hybrid Learning based Medical Image Evaluation (HLMIE), a novel deep learning based cancer cell classification technique. The proposed approach is grounded in traditional learning and classification techniques like Neural Network based Learning and Random Forest Classifier (RFC), and entails creating an automated system to aid doctors in making accurate diagnoses of the various forms of this illness. Acute Myolegenous Leukemia (AML) and Acute-Lymphoblastic-Leukemia (ALL) are the two categories, and they share several symptoms that might make diagnosis difficult. Several techniques involving machine learning and deep learning have been employed in the past to try to make predictions about blood cancer; however these researches have their flaws. Therefore, this research proposes a deep learning/classification logic/medical image processing hybrid model to enhance prediction accuracy. Different degrees of prediction, analysis, and learning methods are incorporated into the suggested hybrid learning model enabled with image processing, and various learning criteria, such as development of learning and assessment precision with regard to epochs, are utilized. In addition, limiting fine-tuning of the system’s output to actual experts and this scheme provides better accuracy in results with respect to better classification performance with prediction logics using hybrid learning methodology, in which the proposed scheme attains 97.84% of prediction accuracy and the reduce the image noise ratio as 2.36% as compared with the conventional classification and learning algorithms. The resulting section shows the proper proof of this quote with exact histographical specification. The resulting summary of the disease prediction is reported properly to the respective care taker or an individual with respect to the principles of trending technology called Internet of Things (IoT).

articleTitle: MR Image Reconstruction from Undersampled Data using Multi Dense Residual Block Network with Spatial and Channel Attention Mechanism and Entropy Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) serves as a leading non-invasive method for medical imaging assessments, finding widespread use in early medical diagnoses due to its exceptional resolution and portrayal of connective softer tissue structures within the human body. Nevertheless, the MRI technique is hindered by an inherently sluggish acquisition procedure. MRI's limitation arises from sequentially acquiring data samples in k-space, with traversal speed constrained by physiological and hardware limitations. Expediting the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) process can be achieved through the application of compressed sensing (CS) which facilitates the reconstruction of high-quality images from k-space data that has been intentionally undersampled. But the conventional CS-MRI approach is associated with prolonged reconstruction times, and the reconstruction process can introduce artifacts, thereby diminishing the overall quality of the reconstruction. To tackle these challenges, in this research, we devised an enhanced model named Multi Dense Residual Block Network with Spatial and Channel Attention Mechanism (MDRBN-SACA), incorporating an entropy function for the proficient reconstruction of MR images. MDRBN optimally utilizes prior image predictions through dense connections among all MDRBs and each MRDB aggregates past predictions and contributes to subsequent MDRBs, ensuring accurate predictions for reconstructing high-quality MR images. Incorporating a spatial and channel attention mechanism into the dense residual network allows for the extraction of details (edges) from the MR image and recreating an image to closely resemble the ground truth image. The assessment of reconstructed image quality among different CNN algorithms utilized different metrics. The outcomes indicate that MDRBNSACA exhibits superior performance across all quantitative metrics compared to other approaches.

articleTitle: Cluster-based Trust Evaluation of Blockchain Miners in Pool Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Blockchain mining has gained popularity since modern technologies started to benefit from its properties such as immutability, secure access, etc. To publish new blocks in Blockchain, miners have to use their resources and participate in the mining process. The majority of miners choose to join a mining pool because they believe that solo mining may be challenging. Due to the existence of many mining pools and the adoption of various incentive mechanisms, they create a lot of confusion for the miners for pool selection. To add a block, miners in the mining pool dedicate their processing power to the consensus process. The pool will get rewards if their efforts are effective. It might be challenging to keep a miner’s assurance throughout the consensus and mining procedures in pool mining. This study, proposed a Trust Model to ensure that the consensus protocol in pool mining will be carried out with trusted miners only. As a result, an innovative approach for trust assessment among the miners is formulated using the ML approach. Instead of allowing all miners, our approach allows only trusted miners into the mining pool for efficient mining. The conceptual framework was implemented using the Hyper ledger tool, and an in-depth evaluation of the performance in terms of transaction per second(tps), transaction validation and commit time was conducted.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease prediction using machine learning involves algorithms that can accurately predict an individual’s risk of heart disease based on their medical history and other risk factors. The current paper introduces a basic effective system designed to diagnose heart disease, which utilizes the Extreme Gradient Boosting technique using a feature selection technique. The system can predict heart disease accurately with a large amount of data. To ensure the effectiveness of the classifier, proper hyperparameter tuning is critical. In this regard, we employed random search, an ideal approach for hyper-parameter optimization, to improve the hyper-parameters of XGBoost. Moreover, the model testing technique called cross-validation was employed to check the efficiency of the prediction of the forecast model. To analyze the proposed algorithm, the researchers compared it to other algorithms. The proposed model has an area under the ROC score of 0.98 and an accuracy of 98 %, outperforming KNN, Naïve Bayes, SVM, Random Forest algorithm in terms of accuracy, positive and negative rates of the model according to the experimental results.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Image Security and Image Steganography Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: In recent days, data transmission has increased a lot and they demand high security protocols for the safe transmission of data. Among the different types of data, images are sensitive as they could carry or represent personal information including medical reports. To transmit images in a safe way, there has been a diverse collection of works in literature. The objective of this paper is to investigate the existing works in terms of image security achieved through cryptographic techniques and steganographic techniques. Image security achieved using cryptographic techniques focus on non-retrievability of the original image from the stego image whereas steganographic techniques focus on hiding the secret information inside a cover medium. We have also recorded the metrics of the different works.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Methods for Underwater Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Enhancing underwater images is a crucial task for numerous purposes such as marine exploration, underwater robotics, and aquatic ecology. Underwater images are degraded due to the complex propagation and scattering of light in water, leading to low contrast, color distortion, blurring, and noise. Compared to conventional methods, deep learning offers superior performance and flexibility for underwater image enhancements in recent years. This research presents a comprehensive examination of deep learning models aimed at enhancing underwater images, including exploration of methods for enhancing underwater images, network architectures, metrics for evaluation and benchmark datasets. We also provide a comprehensive analysis of the cutting-edge techniques on several datasets, emphasizing their respective strengths and limitations. Furthermore, we discuss the systematic investigations for underwater image enhancement, open issues with challenges, and suggest some promising directions for future research.

articleTitle: Advancements in Signal Processing: A Comprehensive Review of Discrete Wavelet Transform and Fractional Wavelet Filter Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: This review paper explores the fundamental importance of fractional wavelet filter (FrWF) and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) techniques in signal processing. These techniques are thoroughly examined and serve as the foundation for many different applications, including data compression, telecommunications, and medical diagnostics. DWT’s multi-resolution analysis, facilitated by breaking signals into various scales, plays a vital role in image compression, denoising, and feature extraction. FrWF, designed for memory-constrained environments, notably reduces memory overhead through external memory utilization. The adaptive memory allocation technique enhances memory efficiency, pivotal for real-time applications like sensors and cameras. These techniques, distinct yet impactful, bolster science and technology. This review highlights their vital roles, progressions, and potential in reshaping memory-restricted signal processing, redefining paradigms.

articleTitle: MS3F: Maximizing Bandwidth and Data Transmission Performance in SUCCESS-HPON Architecture for WDM-PON Using AI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Recent advances in urban and access communication networks have enabled the use of various technologies, with optical transmission mediums and Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) being the most prominent. The SUCCESS-HPON architecture has a WDMPON (Passive Optical Network) component, which necessitates the development of scheduling algorithms. Sequential scheduling with schedule time framing (S3F) algorithms are designed to facilitate efficient, bidirectional connections between the Optical Network Units (ONUs) and Central Office and make sure that the upstream and downstream traffic is organized and sequential. In S3F, Virtual Output Queues (VOQs) are employed as a granting program that consists of timeslots for both upstream and downstream traffic. This helps to reduce the overhead associated with framing and guard bands, while also preserving memory space between traffic flows. The S3F algorithm outperforms the sequentially scheduling algorithm by providing higher throughput, lower delay, and traffic fairness between upstream and downstream traffic. The primary objective of this study is to improve the bandwidth utilization and data transmission performance, the Modified Sequential scheduling with schedule time framing (MS3F) algorithm is enhanced with Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) techniques. Reinforcement learning algorithms can be used to optimize the scheduling decision-making process and dynamically adjust the allocation of resources to improve network efficiency. Deep neural networks can be used to analyze network behavior and predict potential issues, such as network congestion, to improve network reliability. These Artificial Intelligence techniques can help to enhance the performance of the MS3F algorithm by providing more intelligent and efficient scheduling of the WDM-PON traffic.

articleTitle: Noise Reduction in the Capacitive Sensor-Based Tip Clearance Signal from Gas Turbine Engine
publicationTitle: 2023 Second International Conference on Advances in Computational Intelligence and Communication (ICACIC)
abstract: Maintaining optimal tip clearance or tip gap is challenging in the Gas Turbine Engine (GTE). Meanwhile, the rotor blades should not rub the casing. When the capacitive sensor is used to measure the tip clearance in the form of a single peak signal for every blade pass, often the signal will be affected by stationary and non-stationary noises during engine running. This leads to distorted multiple peaks for every blade pass. In this work, the wavelet denoising technique removes the noise, and then the peak frequency in each blade pass is detected through a short-time Fourier transform (STFT). Finally, the cubic spline interpolation technique is employed to obtain the continuous time domain blade pass signal. This work uses the compressor stage of GTE data collected from the Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE), DRDO, Bangalore. From the experimental analysis, this paper observes that the proposed methodology produces substantial results compared to the expected results.
